To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the dialog design problem can be formalized and solved as an optimization problem, (ii) the dialog system can be described as an MDP, and (iii) the optimal strategy for a given dialog system can be found by a combination of supervised learning for estimating the MDP parameters and reinforcement learning for finding the strategy.
it is possible to learn a dialog strategy from data and the MDP model can be used for this purpose.

a dialog system can indeed be modeled as a Markov decision process (MDP) with a simulated user and a simple objective function, and that the MDP model and learning algorithm are effective tools for learning a dialog strategy from a relatively small amount of training data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning a dialog system from a given corpus of dialogs.
developing a formal framework for modeling and optimizing human-machine dialogs, and with the development of algorithms for learning the dialog behavior in such models.
the development and application of a quantitative model for learning the dialog strategies for spoken dialog systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a quantitative model for a dialog system can indeed be formulated and that a data-driven learning of the optimal dialog strategy is feasible in principle.
we are able to show that the proposed framework is indeed a viable alternative to the traditional heuristic approach for dialog strategy design.
our model is able to capture the main aspects of the ATIS dialog and that it is possible to learn an effective strategy with the available training data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that it is possible to use a stochastic model for dialog design and learning.
it is possible to learn dialog strategy in a data driven way, and the learning process is robust enough to work for different applications.
it is possible to formalize and solve the dialog strategy learning problem in a principled way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MDP framework provides a useful formalism that allows us to model the dialog systems in terms of their behavior and the learning of the optimal strategy.
the dialog design process can be automated and that the resulting dialog system can be evaluated in terms of its performance on the criterion.
the MDP framework is a powerful tool that can be used to learn the dialog strategy.
